title: Immunization Services Decision Table: Counting Basis for a Posted Dose Number
content:
Applies to Immunization Services doses posted to a vaccination course after the visit: the dose number the posted dose takes is counted in one of three ways.

**Clause.** Where the course's dose history holds more dose entries than its required doses less its doses still needed account for and Kestrel gave a dose of the course at one of its stores, the number is counted from positions: one past the entries that hold a position once matched registry copies, undocumented entries and live zoster records are set aside. Where the dose history holds no more dose entries than that and Kestrel gave a dose of the course, the number is one past the course's required doses less its doses still needed. Where Kestrel gave no dose of the course, the number is one past every dose entry on it.

## Quantities the table reads

- **Dose entries** — the dose-given entries on the course history before the posting.
- **Doses the account shows as given** — the valid doses the course requires less the valid doses it still needs, both as the course shows them before the posting.
- **Kestrel gave a dose of the course** — at least one dose entry names a Kestrel store.
- **Counted from positions** — the dose entries on the course, where each matched registry copy (a plan-billed entry recorded from another provider matched as a copy of Kestrel's registry report) and each cash-paid entry recorded from another provider without a lot number counts only for the positions it holds, and each live zoster record that is set aside counts for nothing; the posted dose takes the number one past that count.

## Decision table

| Dose entries compared with doses the account shows as given | Kestrel gave a dose of the course | Posted dose number |
|---|---|---|
| More (at least one more) | Yes | One past the positions held |
| Equal or fewer | Yes | One past the doses the account shows as given |
| More | No | One past every dose entry |
| Equal or fewer | No | One past every dose entry |

The threshold is "more than": dose entries equal to the doses the account shows as given fall in the second row, one more falls in the first.

## Hypothetical cases

*Case 1 (hypothetical).* A course requires 2 valid doses and shows 1 still needed, so the account shows 1 as given. The history holds 1 dose entry, naming a Kestrel store. Entries are not more than 1 and Kestrel gave a dose: the posted dose takes number 2.

*Case 2 (hypothetical).* Same account, but the history holds 3 dose entries: one naming a Kestrel store and two recorded from another provider. Entries exceed 1 and Kestrel gave a dose, so the number is counted from positions: one past the entries that hold a position once matched registry copies, undocumented entries and live zoster records are set aside.

*Case 3 (hypothetical).* The history holds 2 dose entries, both recorded from another provider, and no entry names a Kestrel store. The posted dose takes number 3, one past every dose entry, whatever the account shows.
